summary: Monday hooks pass. I added two re-sourced topics for this week's money moments: an airline's profit per passenger (Thanksgiving travel) and Walmart's worker vs CEO (Black Friday). I also added new evidence for the paradox-title challenger.
why: Our figure-free paradox titles about one named person (Arnold 899 views, Musk's jet 928 in a day) match the breakouts' pattern. Workers vs the top lead the channel (McDonald's 1,194). Topics about a company's cut trail by views (Uber 154) but are level on stayed to watch (38.8% vs 39.2%), so I proposed no test.

findings.title: Paradox titles on one named person are our best starts this week
findings.detail: 'Why did Arnold Schwarzenegger work on Twins for free?' 899 views; 'Elon Musk flies a private jet everywhere. Why isn't it his?' 928. I added them to the paradox-title challenger's evidence; stayed to watch isn't in yet.

findings.title: A company's cut vs named people: same stayed to watch
findings.detail: Since 12 Nov, Shorts about named people or workers had 39.2% stayed and about 540 median views; Shorts about a company's cut had 38.8% and about 370. The gap is views, not hold, so there's no challenger.

findings.title: Airlines expect to keep $4.50 per passenger in 2026
findings.detail: IATA, 7 Jun 2026: half of 2025's $9.10, on 5.1 billion passengers. Added as a high-priority topic for Thanksgiving week.

findings.title: Walmart: CEO $29.24M, median associate $30,520 (958 to 1)
findings.detail: FY2026 proxy. The CEO earns a worker's year in about 9 hours. Added for Black Friday week, spaced from Starbucks and McDonald's.

findings.title: Claude: nothing new
findings.detail: Claude Code is still 2.1.330; Fable/Mythos 5.2 are already in seen.json.
